title: They Carried 12 Boys Out of a Flooded Cave Asleep: The Full Thai Cave Rescue
description:
Case 020, the full case file. On 23 June 2018 twelve boys from a junior football team and their coach left their bicycles at the entrance of the Tham Luang cave in Chiang Rai province, northern Thailand, and walked in. Monsoon rain flooded the passages behind them; the bicycles were found at the entrance that evening, still locked. The rising water drove the thirteen deeper, onto a slope of mud far inside the cave. Outside, the search grew to thousands of people: divers worked against the current, pumps were brought in, and for days the rain flooded the passages faster than they could be emptied. The water that was pumped out ran onto rice fields below the mountain, and the farmers accepted it. On 2 July, after nine nights, the British cave divers Rick Stanton and John Volanthen surfaced in a flooded chamber and found all thirteen alive. Thai navy divers and an army doctor then stayed with the group; divers carried letters out, in which the boys told their parents not to worry and the coach apologised. Getting them out was the harder part: the way out lay underwater, through tight, twisting flooded tunnels with a strong current, the oxygen in the chamber was falling and more rain was forecast. Waiting for the water to drop, drilling down from above and teaching the boys to dive were all considered. On 6 July a rescuer, the former Thai navy diver Saman Kunan, who had come back as a volunteer, died while placing air tanks along the route. The plan that was carried out: each boy was sedated (the Australian cave diver Richard Harris is an anaesthetist), fitted with a full-face mask and carried out underwater by a diver. Four boys came out on 8 July, four on 9 July, and the last four boys and their coach on 10 July. A few hours after the last of them was out, with rescue workers still inside, the main pump failed and the water rose again; all of them got out. The team spent about a week in hospital, and later in July boys from the team were ordained as Buddhist novices in honour of Saman Kunan. Rook didn't believe it either.

Animated reconstruction of a true story. The cave mouth, the passages, the chamber, the flooded tunnel, the rescue camp, the rice fields, the hospital ward and the temple hall in the film are generic low-poly sets, not models of the real places; the thirteen, the divers, the rescuers, the doctor, the farmer and the novices are simple figures and nobody's likeness is attempted; clothes, gear and helmets are plain and carry no badge, flag or brand. The cross-section and the chamber cards are diagrams of the idea, not maps, and show no distances or measurements; the oxygen gauge shows no figures. The film does not show how the rescuer died: a light goes out and Rook takes his hat off. Staging details such as the torches, the lock on the bicycle wheel, the pad and pencil, the orange pouch, the case of vials, the silver blankets, the cheering in the camp, the brass torch Rook keeps and the time of day of each scene are reconstruction, not record.

authoring.run: scheduled long run, 17 Nov 2026; the oldest case in the ledger with a scheduled Short, a world3d.py and no long version
authoring.status_reason: ready (uploads as private for the owner), not approved, for two reasons. (1) FACT-CHECK LIMIT: in this run no web page could be opened. Every page fetch was refused ('PROVENANCE_REQUIRED: the permission request for this URL was not answered in time'), including the pages the Short's runs had read; only web search worked, and it returns titles and addresses, not text. So the added facts rest on (a) what the two Short runs read and recorded in the Short's source_notes on 16 Nov 2026 and (b) facts stated outright in the headlines of at least two reputable outlets found today. Nothing was added from memory alone; details that could not be supported this way were left out (see source_notes). The owner should read the sources against the script before making this public. (2) As with the earlier long videos, the film was reviewed from stills and a low-resolution rehearsal, not played at speed or listened to; the first full-resolution 60 fps render is the cloud's.

source_notes: HOW THE ADDED FACTS WERE CHECKED IN THIS RUN (17 Nov 2026). No page could be opened: every fetch came back 'PROVENANCE_REQUIRED, the permission request for this URL was not answered in time' (Wikipedia, Shepton Mallet Caving Club, ABC News/GMA, Reuters on Yahoo, ITV, SCMP, NPR, ABC15 all refused). Web search worked but returns only headlines and addresses. The script therefore uses two kinds of support and nothing else. (A) The Short's own source_notes, written by the two runs that read the pages on 16 Nov 2026 (kept below under 'From the Short'). (B) Headlines found today that state the fact outright, from at least two reputable outlets each. FACT BY FACT. Bicycles left at the entrance and found there that evening, locked: (A) ITV 'bikes are found parked and locked at the cave entrance', Wikipedia 'abandoned bicycles and bags near the entrance'. Monsoon rain flooded the cave behind them; driven deeper onto a muddy slope: (A). The search grew to thousands of people; divers worked against the flood; the rain flooded the passages faster than the pumps could empty them: (A) the Short's notes list 'the thousands of volunteers and soldiers' and 'the pumping operation' among what its runs read and left out for length, and quote ITV, 'flooding underground passages faster than water can be pumped out'. Pumped water flooded rice fields below and the farmers accepted it: (B) Bangkok Post 'Water pumped from Tham Luang flooding nearby farms'; The Nation 'Selfless farmers allow farms to be flooded for cave operation' and 'Farmers register for compensation as cave water submerges rice fields'; The Star/AP 'Thai farmers take on water from cave to help clear exit'. A Bangkok Post headline says 19 farmers turned down aid; one headline only, so it is not in the script. Nine nights until they were found; found on 2 July by Rick Stanton and John Volanthen, all thirteen alive: (A). Thai navy divers and an army doctor stayed with the group: (A) listed in the Short's notes as read and left out ('the navy divers and the army doctor who stayed with the group'); no number of divers and no name is given because none is recorded there. Letters carried out by divers; the boys told their parents not to worry; the coach apologised: (B) CBS News 'Soccer coach apologizes to boys' parents, boys write "don't worry" in letters'; AP on Fox News 'Thai coach apologizes to parents as boys write they're OK'; BBC on RNZ 'Boys tell parents "don't worry" in letters'; Al Jazeera 'Thailand cave boys send letters to their families'; Yahoo News Australia 'Coach of trapped soccer team apologises to parents in letter sent out with divers'. The parents' reply is not in the script (no headline states it). The way out was underwater through tight, twisting passages with a strong current: (A). Oxygen in the chamber was falling and more rain was coming: (A) 'the falling oxygen in the chamber' in the Short's notes; (B) Thai PBS 'Dwindling oxygen and looming rains prompted rescue mission'; N1/CNN 'Thai cave rescuers race against time as oxygen levels drop'; Al Jazeera '"Race against water" as rain threatens Thai cave rescue efforts'. No percentage is narrated or drawn: the gauge on the card has no figures. Options considered (waiting, drilling, teaching the boys to dive, the last judged too risky): (A) Wikipedia via the Short's notes ('teaching them to dive was judged too risky'; 'drilling and waiting were also considered'); (B) ITV 'Thai cave group: What are the rescue options?'. How long a wait would have been and how many shafts were tried are not stated because they were not confirmed. Saman Kunan, a former Thai navy diver, died on 6 July placing air tanks: (A). That he had come back as a volunteer: (B) InDaily/AAP 'Thai volunteer dies during cave rescue effort'; BBC copy 'Ex-navy diver dies on oxygen supply mission'. His age, rank and how he died are not given. Richard Harris, Australian, cave diver and anaesthetist; the boys sedated, in full-face masks, carried out by divers, normally one diver per boy: (A) Wikipedia, CNN Newsource, The New Daily, ABC News via the Short's notes; (B) National Museum of Australia 'Anaesthetist and cave diver'; InDaily 'Adelaide doctor at heart of Thai cave rescue'. The drug is not named in the narration. 8, 9 and 10 July, four, four, and four boys and the coach: (A). The main pump failed a few hours after the last of them was out, with rescue workers still inside, who all got out: (A) NPR 'about three hours', the Telegraph 'a few hours', ABC News 'two hours'; the script says 'a few hours'. Seventeen days: 23 June to 10 July; (A) Reuters' title 'transfixed the world for 17 days'. In hospital, and out about a week later: (B) ABC13/AP 'Thailand soccer team rescued from cave released from hospital'; AFP on Yahoo 'Thailand's cave boys leave hospital for first public appearance'; Euronews, same day. These pages are dated 18 July 2018 in their addresses, eight days after 10 July; because the date itself could only be read from addresses, the film says 'about a week later' and shows no date. Boys from the team ordained as Buddhist novices later that month in honour of the rescuer who died: (B) NPR 'Thai Cave Boys Ordained As Buddhist Novices' (25 July 2018); Reuters on Ahram Online 'Thai cave boys ordained as Buddhist novices to honor dead rescuer'. How many of the boys, and whether the coach was ordained with them, are not stated in the script. LEFT OUT because they could not be supported in this run: the boys' ages and names and the coach's name and age; why they went in; who raised the alarm; a warning sign at the entrance; the length of the cave and how far in they were; what they ate and drank and the meditation; the words exchanged when they were found; the oxygen percentage; numbers of rescuers, divers and pumps and the volume of water; the stretcher relay through the dry part of the cave; how long each dive took; who came out last; later events in the lives of those involved. STAGING THAT IS NOT RECORD: the lock on a bicycle wheel and the worker who finds it, the map table, the row of pumps, the pipe and the look of the fields and the farmer, the foil blankets, the pad and pencil, the orange pouch, the case of vials, the second diver waiting in the tunnel, the cheering in the camp, the workers wading out, the hospital ward, the temple hall with candles and five novices, and the time of day of every scene. FROM THE SHORT (its runs' notes, unchanged): Read for this run (fetched 16 Nov 2026): Wikipedia 'Tham Luang cave rescue' (first part of the article read in full; later sections only in summary and not relied on); Reuters, 'Timeline: Thai cave rescue that transfixed the world for 17 days' (24 June 2019, read on Yahoo News); ITV News, 'How the Thailand cave ordeal unfolded' (10 July 2018); ABC News / Good Morning America, 'With all odds against them, how rescuers pulled off miracle Thai cave mission' (12 July 2018); Shepton Mallet Caving Club, 'A summary of the Tham Luang Rescue' (a caver's day-by-day timeline); CNN Newsource via ABC15, 'Boys rescued from cave in Thailand were sedated with ketamine' (4 April 2019, reporting the rescuers' letter in the New England Journal of Medicine); The New Daily (6 April 2019) on the same letter. Pages that could not be read: BBC, The Guardian, Reuters' own site, AP, NPR, CNN's own site, Britannica, National Geographic, Smithsonian, ABC Australia, History, SBS, the British Cave Rescue Council and the Australian of the Year page (blocked, refused or errors). Every narrated fact is in at least two of the pages read. Twelve boys and their coach went into the cave on 23 June 2018: Wikipedia, Reuters, ITV, ABC News. Rain flooded the cave and trapped them: Wikipedia ('stranded in the tunnels by sudden and continuous rainfall'), Reuters ('rising flood water after heavy rain would soon trap them'), ITV. Bicycles at the entrance: Wikipedia ('abandoned bicycles and bags near the entrance'), ITV ('bikes are found parked and locked at the cave entrance'), ABC News, Shepton. Driven deeper by the water onto a slope of mud: Wikipedia (they fled rising water; found on 'a narrow rock shelf', also called an 'elevated rock'), Reuters ('on a muddy slope'), ABC News ('a small beach'); the film uses the muddy slope. Nine nights: Reuters ('nine nights inside the cave complex'), Wikipedia (found nine days after entering); ABC News counts 'ten days after the group went missing', which is the same span counted inclusively. Divers working against the flood meanwhile: ITV ('flooding underground passages faster than water can be pumped out'), Reuters, Shepton. Found on 2 July by the British divers Rick Stanton and John Volanthen, all thirteen alive: all five timeline sources. The way out was through flooded passages and some of the boys could not swim: Wikipedia ('It was believed that some of the group could not swim'; teaching them to dive was judged too risky), ABC News ('most of them did not know how to swim'); the film says 'some', which both support. Saman Kunan, a former Thai navy diver, died on 6 July while placing air tanks: Wikipedia, Reuters, ABC News ('delivering extra air tanks'), ITV (unnamed), Shepton ('to stage cylinders'). Sedated, in full-face masks, carried out by divers one at a time: Wikipedia (ketamine given by the anaesthetist Richard Harris; 'positive pressure full-face mask'), CNN Newsource ('given unspecified doses of ketamine', 'full-face masks supplying oxygen', 'while we were carrying them out'), The New Daily, ABC News ('normally one diver per boy'). Out over three days, 8 to 10 July, four, four and five: Wikipedia, Reuters, ITV, ABC News. Hours after the last of them was out the pumping failed and the water rose: ABC News ('Just two hours after the last rescue was made ... the pumps ... broke down'), Shepton (at 21:10, after the last boy reached the entrance at 18:53, 'a water pipe coupling breaks causing the water to rise rapidly'), Wikipedia ('a water pipe burst and the main pump stopped working'). Conflicts and things kept out of the film. Distance: Wikipedia's lead says about 2 km from the entrance, ABC News 2.9 miles, Shepton about 4 km plus 750 m, so no distance is narrated or drawn and the cross-section card says NOT TO SCALE. What they sat on: rock shelf, muddy slope or small beach, see above. Kunan's age and rank differ between pages (37 or 38; petty officer, later promoted), so neither is given. The cause of the water rising at the end is a failed pump in two sources and a broken pipe coupling in the third; the narration says 'the pumps fail', which two support, and the description says 'the pumping failed'. The exchange usually quoted from the divers' video ('How many of you?' 'Thirteen.' 'Brilliant.') was found verbatim in only one page read, so it is not quoted: Rook counts instead. 'Almost no food' and the coach leading meditation were each confirmed in only one page read and were cut from the script. Whether the boys were fully unconscious differs (Wikipedia 'fully unconscious'; the journal reports say sedated), so the film says 'sedate'. The first script draft said 'the only way out is underwater' and 'the cave floods again'; both were softened to 'the way out is underwater' and 'the water rises again' because drilling and waiting were also considered and the sources describe water rising in the inner chambers, not the whole cave. Left out for length: the thousands of volunteers and soldiers, the pumping operation and the water diverted on the mountain, the falling oxygen in the chamber, the navy divers and the army doctor who stayed with the group, the order in which the boys came out (disputed), the boys' ages and names, and the later lives of those involved. Staging choices that are not facts: the number of bicycles (five are shown), the boys' torches and the torch that goes out, the low arch and the boulder, the tally marks, the silver blanket, the stretcher under a foil blanket, the work lights, the small brass torch Rook keeps, the colours of shirts and helmets, and the time of day of each scene. Second check, by the run that took this case over after the first run was cut off (16 Nov 2026): four more pages were read against the script, namely HISTORY.com 'Last of Thai soccer team rescued from cave' (10 July entry), NPR 'Pump Fails At Thai Cave Hours After Soccer Boys Rescued' (11 July 2018), the Telegraph report carried by Yahoo News 'Thailand cave rescue: Water pumps failed just after last boy escaped' and the South China Morning Post's account of the divers' interviews. They confirm: entry on 23 June and the monsoon flood (HISTORY, NPR); found alive on 2 July by two British divers after a nine-day search (HISTORY; NPR and the Telegraph give the date); the escape was underwater through 'dangerous, tight and twisting passageways, with strong currents' (HISTORY) and 'twisting, jagged submerged corridors in swirling murky waters' (Telegraph); Saman Kunan, a former Thai navy SEAL, died on 6 July delivering air tanks (HISTORY, Telegraph); the boys were sedated and wore full-face masks (HISTORY); out on 8, 9 and 10 July, all thirteen alive (HISTORY, NPR, SCMP); the main pump failed about three hours (NPR), 'a few hours' (Telegraph), 'just hours' (SCMP) after the last of them was out, while rescue workers were still inside; all of those got out. Changed because of this check: the line 'some of these boys can't even swim' was cut. The first run had it from Wikipedia ('it was believed that some of the group could not swim') and ABC News ('most'), but none of the four pages read in the second check states it, and it was reported after the rescue that the coach said all of the boys could swim; a disputed claim is not narrated as fact. The line now says the way out is 'through tight, twisting tunnels in a strong current', which HISTORY and the Telegraph both support, and the label on those shots reads UNDERWATER. The description no longer calls the coach an assistant coach because only some pages do. 'Nine nights' counts 23 June to 2 July, the time until they were found (Reuters, and HISTORY's nine-day search); it is not the whole time in the cave, which was 17 or 18 days depending on the page. 'One by one' means each boy was dived out individually with his own diver, four on each of the first two days and five on the last; it does not mean one a day. The boy who pulls his foot back from the water is staging, not record.

shown_moments.Saman Kunan dies placing air tanks: shots 41 to 43 (a diver stands a tank by the line; his lamp dims; the light by the tanks goes out). The death itself is not shown.

experiments.E1_E2: Spine v2. The cold open is not the Short's (the walk into the cave) but the least believable image of the whole case: a sleeping boy in a mask taken under water. Rook's doubt is spoken at the water's edge with the bubbles still coming up (no office). The film then goes back to 23 June for 11 seconds and runs forward; dates and places are on-screen labels.
experiments.setup_shortened: plan/learnings.json asks long-form for a shorter setup and a stronger mid-video reversal. The walk in and the flood are 26 s of 176 s; the reversal ('finding them was the easy part', the oxygen, the options, the death of a rescuer) starts at 83.9 s, 48% of the runtime, and the plan from the cold open returns at 115 s.
experiments.rook_action: Detective actions: he counts the thirteen along the ledge with a wingtip (28) and sounds the water with a weighted line (40). Mannerisms: beak tap (6, 19, 37), hat jump (28, 56), hat tipped to the farmer (23), brim down (32, 70), hat to chest (44, 65), pocketing the brass torch (70). He makes no joke from the death of the rescuer onward except the plain 'I was wrong' of the ending.

sound_plan.first_frame: One 'hit' at 0.08 s with the diver taking hold, then a splash and bubbles as they go under; no music sting.
sound_plan.music: The engine's score follows the segment moods: hook, tense for the doubt, calm for the start, tense for the rain, action for the climb, tense for the search, calm for the farmers, tense for the nights, wonder for the finding, calm for the letters, tense for the re-hook and the options, sad for Saman Kunan and for Rook's hat (the sad mood carries no drum loop), tense for the plan, action for the dive, triumph for the three days, tense for the pump, calm for the hospital, sad for the novices, end.
sound_plan.hush: Shot 53 (the squeeze): the music drops out for the breath before 'Four boys come out that day'.
sound_plan.voice: am_fenrir, ducked over the bed by the engine; measured in the local rehearsal, not listened to.

quality_gate.access: Inspected: low-res contact sheets of every 3D shot (three rounds: all 61 3D shots, then 24, then 6 changed shots), the seven flat cards at two points each with the caption band marked, the thumbnail at full size (three versions), four shots at 1280x720 and 20 samples, and a full-length rehearsal (384x216, 4 samples, 6 fps 3D frames composited at 12 fps with captions, labels, overlays, inserts and sound) reviewed as a 2-frames-per-second sheet of the whole video (352 frames), with the changed parts rendered and reviewed again twice. Not done: no playback at speed; the audio was measured, not listened to. The cloud render is the first full-resolution 60 fps pass.
quality_gate.method: Round 1 (all shots). Found: the rescue camp and the night shots far too dark and the camera too far away; the fields never showed water; the workers at the map table had their backs to the camera and hid Rook; cameras inside rock in two shots (the workers wading out, the second tunnel shot); the hospital ward washed out to white with tiny figures; Rook hidden behind the coach; a lantern stand across the lens in the temple; the wide chamber shot too small in a wide frame. Round 2 (24 shots): all of those restaged or relit; left: Rook cut off the top of the frame in two flying shots, the tunnel camera still in a rock. Round 3 (6 shots) and the thumbnail. Round 4 (rehearsal, 2 fps sheet): the captions sit lower in 16:9 than the cards allowed for, so five card texts (NOT TO SCALE, RUNNING DOWN, TOO RISKY, ALL THIRTEEN, 13 OF 13) ran under the captions and were moved up; three segments had the picture a beat behind the words (the plan, the pump, the ending) and were retimed; Rook was still cut off flying out of the cave. Round 5 (rehearsal of the changed parts): the gate FAILED locally on a static stretch at 118 to 122 s (the diver kneeling by the case, held 3.9 s). Fixed in the film, not in the gate: the shot was shortened and a close-up of a gloved hand lifting a vial was added. Round 6: the ending retimed so that the camp is on screen for 'thousands of people' and the board for 'thirteen in, thirteen out'; the silver blankets, which read as boulders at full resolution, were made smaller.
quality_gate.gate_result: Last rehearsal, from the final storyboard: local gate PASS. 70 shots, mean 2.52 s, longest 3.85 s, first shot 2.8 s with a hit at 0.08 s; Rook acts in 32 of 70 shots (46%); -14.6 LUFS, peak -1.1 dBFS, voice 16.1 dB over the bed; closest match to any earlier episode 0.70 (limit 0.93). Duration 176.4 s. One shot (the silver blankets) was changed after that rehearsal and checked as a still only.
quality_gate.checked: Every kind in the storyboard exists in world3d.SHOTS3D or scenes.SHOTS (by script); HOST lists every kind in which Rook is placed; no kind is used more than three times (camp_wide three times from three angles; take_under, mask_on and carry_in twice) and none twice in a row; one hush (shot 53); re-hook at 83.9 s of 176.4 s (48%). On-screen dates and names (23 JUNE 2018, THAM LUANG, THAILAND, 2 JULY 2018, 6 JULY 2018, SAMAN KUNAN, 8 JULY 2018, 8/9/10 JULY, 8 TO 10 JULY 2018, 10 JULY 2018, NINE NIGHTS, 13 OF 13) are all in the Short's verified notes; the hospital and the ordination carry no date. Nothing graphic is shown; no badge, flag, emblem, medical or religious symbol, lettering or likeness appears in the sets.
quality_gate.not_met: Loudness range measures 2.9 LU (ffmpeg ebur128) against the checklist's 4 LU; this is the engine's mix. Preview at full resolution was done for four shots only. Full-resolution frames took 40 to 60 s each on this 2-core machine; the previous long (r019) measured the same here (38 to 70 s), so this film is no heavier than what the pipeline already renders. The fact-check limit is described in authoring.status_reason.

review.weakest: The water from the pipe is a stream of tan blocks and does not read well as water; the boys in the ward and the novices are simple props, not jointed figures, and barely move; several chamber shots share one look; the crowd in the camp is small for 'thousands'; the lock on the bicycle is hard to see; low-poly hands cannot really hold the pencil, the pouch or the vial. Respect and accuracy is scored 4, not 5, only because the added facts could not be re-read on the pages in this run.
